question: Holding the V20 anonymous structural state and consequence definition fixed, does refining Hebrew operator identity from Strong's lemma to independently supplied OSHB morphological realization recover a broad transferable context-conditioned operator effect; and does any rescued Hebrew representation align with the already-frozen glyph context-modulation profile without one-to-one operator matching?
claimBoundary: A positive result supports the claim that the Hebrew operator unit used in V20 was too coarse under this projector, if a morphology-refined representation passes sealed holdout and control and improves over lemma on paired parent lemmas. Cross-system profile alignment, if it also passes, supports similarity in which anonymous structural contexts expose operator modulation. It does not establish lexical translation, Hebrew-glyph symbol identity, historical contact, common authorship, theology, phonetics, English glosses, or that OSHB morphology is itself the recovered underlying grammar.

hebrewSource.baseTokenIdentity: first numeric lemma component rendered H<number>
hebrewSource.morphAlignment: split lemma and morph attributes on slash; use the morph segment aligned to the first numeric lemma component; if absent use <MISSING>

fixedStructuralTarget.state: exact V20 anonymous equality pattern of the previous four BASE LEMMA tokens, padded by <START>; morphology never changes the state label
fixedStructuralTarget.consequence: exact V20 consequence computed only from the BASE LEMMA sequence; morphology never changes SAME/REPEAT/SEEN/NEW/END classification
fixedStructuralTarget.sharedStates: inherit the exact shared-state set frozen by V20; V21 may not reselect states

lemma.status: exact inherited V20 Hebrew operator representation and baseline model

lemmaCoarseMorph.coarseFamily: after optional H language prefix, N/V/A/P/T/S families keep first two characters; other families keep first character; missing is <MISSING>
lemmaCoarseMorph.source: aligned OSHB morph segment on each occurrence

lemmaFullMorph.source: exact aligned OSHB morph segment on each occurrence, stripped only of surrounding whitespace; missing is <MISSING>

training.eligibility: TRAIN only; refined identities are ranked by train frequency then identity, and only the frozen cap may be retained

models.lemma: reuse exact V20 frozen Hebrew model without refitting
models.refinedInvariant: for each refined operator r, Pinv(y|S,r) is V20's invariant-operator construction: V20-style state baseline multiplied by the TRAIN-smoothed refined-operator-wide outcome ratio and renormalized
models.refinedContextConditioned: Pctx(y|S,r) learned from TRAIN (S,r) outcome counts and hierarchically smoothed toward refined Pinv; low-support pairs collapse exactly to Pinv
models.primaryWithinRepresentationContrast: log2 Pctx(observed y|S,r) - log2 Pinv(observed y|S,r)
models.withinRepresentationNull: for each refined operator, permute its frozen TRAIN interaction-residual blocks across the inherited V20 shared states while leaving that occurrence's Pinv fixed
models.pairedRefinementContrast: on evaluation occurrences covered by both the inherited lemma model and a refined model, compare refined Pctx-vs-Pinv context gain with the inherited lemma Pctx-vs-Pinv gain; average occurrence differences within base lemma first, then across eligible base lemmas
models.pairedRefinementNull: independent sign flip of each eligible base lemma's paired refined-minus-lemma mean difference; exact enumeration when feasible, otherwise 4096 deterministic sign-flip permutations

contextProfile.definition: for each inherited V20 shared state, average realized Pctx-vs-Pinv gain within operator first and then across evaluable operators having events in that state
contextProfile.similarity: Pearson correlation of Hebrew representation and inherited V20 glyph state-gain profiles over identical anonymous V20 structural-state labels
contextProfile.null: exactly permute glyph state-profile labels relative to Hebrew when feasible; otherwise 4096 deterministic permutations

evaluation.rescueRule: A morphology-refined representation rescues Hebrew context conditioning only if it passes the within-representation gate in BOTH holdout and control AND its paired refinement advantage over inherited lemma passes in BOTH lanes. Narrow subset success is blocked by the frozen parent-coverage requirement.
evaluation.crossSystemRule: A rescued Hebrew representation additionally aligns with glyph contexts only if the inherited glyph V20 model passes its within-system gate in both lanes and that representation's context-profile comparison with glyph passes in both lanes.
